title: Keryx shell hook configuration
description: planned — Declares the lifecycle hook registrations read by `keryx shell`'s own hook runtime (W6): `~/.keryx/hooks.json` (user scope) and `.metaproject/hooks.json` (project scope), merged over Keryx's built-in registrations by the precedence in workstreams/W6-shell-hooks.md (built-in < user < project). No runtime reads this shape yet; it is the target contract for the hook runtime described there. Field and I/O-contract naming intentionally mirrors the public Claude Code hooks convention (stdin JSON, exit-code semantics, stdout JSON decision) so the same hook command can run unmodified under `keryx shell` and under a host harness's own hook installer.

schemaVersion.description: Config format version. Bumped only on a breaking shape change; a consumer must fail closed (refuse to load, not silently ignore) on an unrecognised major.

_keryxManaged.description: Sentinel block Keryx writes into a file it manages so `keryx hooks enable|disable` and doctor/uninstall can distinguish Keryx-owned entries from a human's own edits without deleting the latter. Present only on the merged project/user artifact `keryx hooks` itself writes, never required on a hand-authored source file. Intentionally shaped as an object here, not the string/string-array sentinel some host settings files (e.g. `.claude/settings.json`) use, because this file must record per-entry `managedHookIds` for `keryx hooks enable|disable` to target individually, which a bare marker string cannot express.

version.description: Keryx CLI version that last wrote this block.

managedHookIds.description: Hook registration ids this file's Keryx-managed block currently owns, so a later `keryx hooks disable` removes exactly those entries.

hooks.description: One array of hook registrations per lifecycle event. Unknown event keys are rejected (additionalProperties: false) so a typo fails closed instead of silently registering nothing.

hookList.description: Registrations for this event, in the deterministic execution order defined by workstreams/W6-shell-hooks.md (built-ins first by fixed id order, then user-scope, then project-scope, each in file order; ties broken by `id`).

hookRegistration.description: Either a full registration (all required fields, `id` without the `keryx.` prefix, and no `acknowledge`) or a project/user disable override of a built-in (`id` with the `keryx.` prefix, `enabled: false`, optionally `acknowledge`) — see the `oneOf` below. Disable overrides of a built-in GATE (class `gate`/`gate-advisory`) are ignored at project scope (a project file can never turn one off) and, at user scope, need `acknowledge: "disable-builtin-gate"` or they are ignored too; `observe`/`context` built-ins may be disabled from either scope without `acknowledge`.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within one event's list after merge. Built-in ids are namespaced `keryx.<name>` (e.g. `keryx.ctx-guard`) so a project/user id can never collide with or silently shadow a built-in. A project/user file may use a `keryx.<name>` id only in the disable-override form (`{id, enabled: false}`, see `oneOf`) — never in a full registration.

acknowledge.description: Only in a USER-scope disable override of a built-in gate (class gate or gate-advisory): the operator's explicit acknowledgement that the gate is turned off. Without it the override is ignored with a warning. A project file can never disable a built-in gate.

description.description: Human-readable purpose, shown by `keryx hooks list`.

matcher.description: Tool-name filter for PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure (regex over the tool name, e.g. `Bash|Write|Edit`); ignored (must be `"*"`) for events that are not per-tool (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, SessionEnd).

class.description: `gate`: this hook's decision can tighten the policy-engine outcome (deny/ask/add-context) and its failure semantics follow the fail-closed row in workstreams/W6-shell-hooks.md's failure table, fail-closed in every profile. `gate-advisory`: same tightening power as `gate` when it runs successfully, but its failure semantics are profile-aware — fail-open with a recorded warning in `read-only-review` and `monitored-trusted-local`, fail-closed in `unattended-untrusted` (see the failure-semantics table). `observe`: side-effect-free (e.g. a learning/evidence recorder); it can never change the outcome and its failure is always fail-open-with-warning, regardless of profile. `context`: may add `additionalContext` but never a decision; failure is always fail-open.

command.description: The hook process to run. Always a command; there is no in-process/prompt/HTTP handler type in v1 (see workstreams/W6-shell-hooks.md Design > Non-goals).

argv.description: Argv vector, e.g. ["keryx", "security", "check-input"]. Never shell-interpolated; spawned directly to close the command-injection-via-interpolation class W8 audits for.

cwd.description: Working directory, resolved relative to the project root. Defaults to the project root.

env.description: Extra environment entries. Merged over the fixed env allowlist described in workstreams/W6-shell-hooks.md Execution; a key not on that allowlist and not listed here is stripped, not merely unset.

timeoutMs.description: Hard wall-clock budget for one invocation. A hook that exceeds it is killed and treated as a timeout failure (see failure-semantics table).

runsIn.description: `sandbox` (default): spawned through the existing OS sandbox adapter (src/harness/process/sandbox), no network unless `network` is set. `unsandboxed` requires the profile's `requiredControls.isolation` to allow it and is refused otherwise (fail closed).

network.description: Network posture for the hook's sandbox, reusing the sandbox's own two-state model. Never `full`; a hook that needs broader egress is out of scope for v1.

appliesToChildAgents.description: Whether a spawned Keryx subagent inherits this registration as part of its explicit parent hook set (see workstreams/W6-shell-hooks.md Design > Child agents). A child never inherits a host harness's own ambient hooks, mirroring the --safe-mode rationale for external claude -p children.

profiles.description: Security profiles this registration is active under. Omitted or empty means all profiles.

enabled.description: Set to false by `keryx hooks disable <id>` without deleting the registration, so re-enabling restores prior config exactly.
